title: Accelerator pool cross-zone upgrade safety, handoff and hybrid autoscale
creator: Omar Rahman
description: Objective: Build a reusable Terraform module and upgrade orchestration pattern for accelerator (GPU) node pools deployed inside customer VPCs that supports hybrid autoscaling (ASG + Karpenter) across zones, safe driver/runtime upgrades, and production-grade healthchecks. Scope: - Terraform module API for defining cross-zone accelerator pools (subnet affinity, instance profile, taints/labels) - Orchestration recipe for driver (NVIDIA/AMDx) and kubelet upgrades with preflight checks and rollback hooks - Healthcheck DaemonSet and control-plane alerts (node readiness, GPU driver probe, pod eviction rates) - Hybrid autoscaling configuration supporting reserved ASG capacity + Karpenter burst lane - Migration and handoff tooling for clusters currently using only ASG Non-goals: - Rewriting Karpenter controller; we integrate with current upstream. - Implementing new online-driver hotpatching (we will sequence node replacements). Success metrics: - zero >5-minute customer-facing incidents during staged upgrade on internal test clusters - <1% increase in pod evictions sustained over 6 hours during canary - automated upgrade rollback triggers work in <10 minutes after health failure Constraints / considerations: - Must operate inside customer-managed VPCs without modifying CNI or ENI allocations - Respect tenant RBAC and optionally use customer KMS for bootstrap secrets - Support mixed instance types for cost/availability optimization - Keep Terraform module inputs concise to avoid multi-variant combinatorial testing Compatibility: - Kubernetes 1.25+ (verify kubelet flags) - Karpenter v0.33+ and ASG workflows on AWS - NVIDIA and AMD GPU driver families (install via DaemonSet or host-level package) Artifacts: - Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Accelerator+Pool+Module - Terraform module: github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules//modules/accelerator-pool - Draft PR for orchestration recipe: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/3456
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes stable inputs for subnet selection, instance families, taints, labels, and upgrade policy
Module produces ASG and Karpenter provisioning hooks without requiring customer-level controller changes
End-to-end upgrade runbook (canary -> staggered -> rollback) validated on internal staging cluster
Healthcheck DaemonSet reports node GPU readiness and driver version; alerts created in Grafana/Alertmanager
Documentation and API examples added to the private-deployments docs site
implementation_notes: Design the module to emit a cloud-init + S3-stored bootstrap script for driver installation to keep Terraform idempotent
Provide two upgrade strategies: 'staggered-replace' (preferred) and 'blue-green' (for critical disruptions), selectable by input
Add lifecycle ignore_changes for ASG launch template tags that downstream tooling may mutate
Use node annotation 'accelerator.redwood.io/upgrade-phase' to coordinate drain/cordon across Karpenter and ASG reconcilers
Expose a boolean input 'enable_karpenter_burst' default false to avoid surprising customers during initial rollout
rollout_plan: 1) Merge Terraform module to main and publish tag v0.1.0
2) Deploy to internal-staging cluster (three AZs) with enable_karpenter_burst=false
3) Run non-disruptive preflight (kernel, nvidia-smi probe) against all nodes
4) Start canary upgrade: replace 1 AZ at a time using staggered-replace, monitor 2h
5) If metrics stable, continue staggered rollout across remaining nodes
6) If failure, trigger automated rollback (revert ASG launch template and re-create nodes using previous AMI) and run postmortem
monitoring_and_alerts: Grafana dashboard: Accelerator Pools — per-pool GPU utilization, pod evictions, node readiness
Alert: accelerator.node-driver-failure -> fires when >2 nodes in pool report driver-probe=false for 10m
Alert: accelerator.upgrade-eviction-surge -> fires when pod evictions in pool >5% baseline over 15m
SLOs to measure: average node replace time, % successful automated rollbacks
test_plan: Unit test: Terraform plan diff coverage for all major input permutations
Integration: create temporary VPC cluster in CI, deploy module, verify ASG + Karpenter coexistence
Chaos test: simulate AZ outage during upgrade to ensure fallback lane is respected
Driver compatibility test: run GPU test job matrix (CUDA 12 / ROCm) inside upgraded nodes
